checkpoints.description: [1/5] Plan: zero-dependency focus timer with a themed static UI under the aikit ui guard

impact_assessment.why: exercise the UI contract, snapshot and style gates on a fresh project with a real, reviewable UI surface
impact_assessment.benefits: a usable local focus timer; a worked example of a non-React zero-dependency UI contract with an inventory proof and theme tokens
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ui.json surface and protected paths must match the real tree or verify refuses every edit; dependency: stdlib only, no npm or test runner beyond unittest; concurrency: session store written from a single-threaded http.server, one writer at a time; state: sessions.json must survive power loss mid-write
impact_assessment.mitigation: scaffold the contract from the real tree after the UI exists; atomic temp+fsync+replace writes with a schema version and refusal on unknown versions; unit tests under 10ms with no spawns and integration tests under 350ms

[1/4] Plan: Audio chimes, customizable intervals, and session analytics with zero external dependencies

impact_assessment.why: Fulfill user request for phase transition audio chimes, configurable interval durations on the fly, and local session analytics/history while preserving Tempo's zero-dependency, crash-safe architecture.
impact_assessment.benefits: Rich user feedback via Web Audio API without asset bloat; full user autonomy over focus and break lengths without restarting Python; local session history and analytics; 100% test coverage and UI guard compliance.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI contract surface changes must be tracked through .aikit/ui.json without breaking inventory proofs; dependency: stdlib and native Web Audio API only, no external audio files or libraries; concurrency: single-threaded HTTP server writes must remain atomic; state: session.json additions must be backward-compatible with schema 1 or safely migrated without data loss.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep all audio generation purely synthetic in client JS; validate all interval inputs on backend before saving; maintain atomic fsync+replace session persistence with backward-compatible schema; follow strict TDD and UI guard begin/verify/finish cycle.
